blog.titolo: What does a social media manager do?

blocchi.titolo: What social media is for, for a brand
blocchi.testo: A brand uses social media for different goals: getting known (awareness), building a relationship with people (community), bringing visits to the website and sales, giving support. Each goal is measured differently, so it has to be chosen before publishing. The social media manager works mainly on organic content, meaning content that isn't sponsored.
blocchi.esempio: For the iced teas, Cinque Foglie's goal is to get the new range known; for matcha, to build a community of people sharing their recipes.

domande.testo: Match each goal to how it's measured.
coppie: Reach: how many people see the posts
Visits and purchases from the link
domande.spiegazione: First the goal, then the right number to watch.

blog.titolo: What does a social media manager do?

blocchi.titolo: Each platform has its own audience
blocchi.testo: Platforms differ in audience and format. Instagram lives on photos, carousels and short videos (reels). TikTok on short, spontaneous videos, discovered mostly through the algorithm's recommendations. Facebook on groups and communities. LinkedIn on work and professions. Pinterest on saved ideas and inspiration. You don't need to be everywhere: better a few platforms done well, where your audience is.
blocchi.esempio: Cinque Foglie chooses Instagram (recipes and curated photos) and Pinterest (gift and iced tea ideas), and doesn't open a LinkedIn account: its customers don't look for tea there.

domande.testo: A tea brand with a small team. What's best?

opzioni.t: A few platforms where its audience is, done well
Opening an account on every platform
Publishing the exact same post everywhere

domande.spiegazione: Better less and done well, adapting formats to each platform.

blog.titolo: What does a social media manager do?

blocchi.testo: Organic content is published for free and mainly reaches people who follow the account or who get it from the algorithm. Sponsored content (social ads) is paid for to reach people chosen by age, interests, location. It's often handled by another role or an agency, but the social media manager chooses which content deserves a boost.
blocchi.esempio: The cold brew reel got lots of saves organically: it's a good candidate to sponsor, to show it to people who don't know Cinque Foglie yet.

domande.testo: An organic post always reaches all of the account's followers.
domande.spiegazione: Only some see it: the algorithm decides who to show it to.

blog.titolo: What does a social media manager do?

blocchi.testo: Every platform decides what to show each person with an algorithm that tries to predict what will interest them. It looks at signals such as how long people spend on content, whether they watch to the end, and whether they save, share or comment. There's no secret trick: content people find useful or beautiful gets shown more.
blocchi.esempio: A carousel «5 mistakes to avoid with matcha» gets saved a lot because it's useful: the algorithm shows it to more people.

domande.testo: Which signals tell the algorithm that people like a piece of content?

opzioni.t: They watch it to the end
It has lots of identical hashtags repeated

domande.spiegazione: Saves, shares, watch time and comments count; stuffing it with hashtags doesn't.

blog.titolo: How social media algorithms work, explained simply

blocchi.testo: To avoid posting at random, you choose three or four fixed themes, the content pillars. Every post belongs to one of the pillars. That way the account is recognisable and there's always an idea to start from.
blocchi.esempio: Cinque Foglie's pillars: «Learn about tea» (how to brew it), «Recipes» (iced teas, matcha latte), «Behind the scenes» (growers, packaging), «The community» (customers' photos).

domande.testo: A post «How to choose the right teapot» belongs to the pillar…
domande.spiegazione: It explains something to the audience: it's educational content.

blog.titolo: How to build a social media content calendar

blocchi.testo: The same theme can be told in different formats. Short vertical videos (reels, TikTok) to get discovered. Carousels, meaning several images to swipe through, to explain step by step: they get saved often. Stories, which last 24 hours, for everyday updates and quick questions. Single posts for a strong photo or an announcement. You choose the format based on what you want to achieve.
blocchi.esempio: The iced tea recipe becomes a 20-second reel to get discovered and a carousel with the quantities to save.

domande.testo: Match each format to its typical use.
coppie: Explaining step by step, to be saved
Daily updates that disappear after 24 hours

blog.titolo: How to build a social media content calendar

blocchi.testo: The content calendar says what gets published, where and when, usually a few weeks ahead. It brings together key dates (launches, holidays, seasons), pillars and formats. Posting regularly matters more than posting a lot. Always leave some room for things that happen unexpectedly.
blocchi.esempio: Cinque Foglie's October: evening herbal teas on Mondays, recipes on Thursdays, behind the scenes on Saturdays; the advent calendar at the end of the month.

domande.testo: Put the steps of preparing a calendar in order.
voci: Set the month's goals and key dates
Assign a format and day to each piece of content
domande.spiegazione: First the why and the when, then the what and the how.

blocchi.titolo: Other people's content, rights and accessibility
blocchi.testo: Content created by customers (UGC, user-generated content) is valuable, but before reposting it you ask for permission and credit the author. Music and images have rights too: only use those with a suitable licence, such as the platforms' music libraries for commercial use. Good content is also accessible: subtitles on videos and image descriptions (alt text) for people who can't see.
blocchi.esempio: A customer posts a beautiful photo of her matcha latte: Cinque Foglie writes to ask if it can repost it and credits her in the post.

domande.testo: What do you do before reposting a customer's photo?

opzioni.t: Repost it straight away, it's public anyway
Remove her name from the photo

domande.spiegazione: Public content isn't free to use: you need the author's permission.

Each format has a use: video to get discovered, carousels to explain, stories for everyday updates.

opzioni.t: Posting only when you have time

finali.spiegazione: Better regular than lots and at random.

opzioni.t: Making them understandable without sound and for people who can't hear

finali.spiegazione: Accessibility: many people watch without sound, and some people can't hear.

blocchi.testo: Reach: how many different people saw a piece of content. Impressions: how many times it was seen in total, including repeat views by the same person. Interactions: likes, comments, saves, shares. Link clicks: how many people went to the website. Follower growth: how many new followers in the period. Saves and shares usually say more than likes, because they take more effort.
blocchi.esempio: A carousel has a reach of 4,000 and 6,000 impressions: some people saw it more than once.

coppie: Different people who saw the content
People who want to find it again

blog.titolo: Social media metrics: which to watch and when

blocchi.testo: Engagement rate shows how much people react to content: interactions divided by reach, times 100. It can also be calculated on followers, which is useful for comparing different accounts, but when you know the reach it's better to use it. There's no right value for everyone: compare with your own previous posts.
blocchi.esempio: A reel has 225 interactions and a reach of 5,000 people: 225 / 5,000 × 100 = 4.5%.

domande.testo: A post has 90 interactions and a reach of 3,000. Engagement rate on reach?

blog.titolo: Engagement rate: what it is and how to calculate it

blocchi.testo: Managing the community means replying to comments and messages, thanking, helping, moderating. You reply quickly and on brand, even to criticism. Only spam and insults are hidden or reported, not honest criticism. Repeated questions become ideas for new content.
blocchi.esempio: Three people ask in one week «how much matcha for one cup?»: a kind reply to all of them and, the following Monday, a carousel with the quantities.

domande.testo: A customer criticises a late delivery in a comment. What do you do?

opzioni.t: Reply quickly, apologise and message them privately to sort it out
Don't reply, so as not to give it visibility

domande.spiegazione: Honest criticism is handled with a quick reply, not deleted.

blog.titolo: Community management: what to answer and what to hide

blocchi.titolo: The rules: ads, giveaways and privacy
blocchi.testo: If content is advertising, it must be clear: in paid partnerships with creators you use the platforms' labels and tools (for example «paid partnership», #ad). In Italy, prize contests («comment to win…») have precise legal rules (Presidential Decree 430/2001): before running one, ask whoever handles it in the company. And the data of people who write privately is handled under the GDPR.
blocchi.esempio: Cinque Foglie gives a creator a kit in exchange for a reel: the reel must be labelled as a partnership, even if no money changed hands.

domande.testo: Free products given in exchange for a post must be disclosed as advertising.
domande.spiegazione: A free product in exchange for content is also a commercial partnership to disclose.

domande.testo: You want to run a «comment and win». What do you do first?

opzioni.t: Check the prize contest rules with whoever handles them
Run it only in stories, so it doesn't count

domande.spiegazione: In Italy prize contests are regulated by law.

blog.titolo: Ads, giveaways and privacy on social media: the rules in Italy
